paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.

annotations.annotation: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various configurations measured in percentage. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled as "embedding", "1st layer", "random layers" and additional variations, "random" and additional variations and culminating with "unperturbed." The vertical axis labeled as "Accuracy", with a linear scale ranging from 70 to 95, marked at intervals of 5. Each category on the horizontal axis is represented by a bar of different colors: blue for "embedding" and "1st layer", green for "random layers" and its subcategories, red for "random" variations, and orange for "unperturbed". The bars depict varying heights with the "embedding" and "1st layer" bars showing values around 80, and "unperturbed" being the tallest at about 92. The "random layers" category bars are generally similar to blue bars, values around 80. The arrangement of the categories is neither explicitly alphabetical nor descending but based on specific configurations. The "random" category bars are generally shorter, with the red bars having values around 70.
